cells.tense: You're seeing it now, at the very start of it.
cells.verb: seeing clearly at the threshold, before there's anything yet to cut
cells.place: where something is growing and needs your care
cells.ask: offer one more step of tending than feels entirely safe — let the seeing feed the care, and what comes back is a light that shines from you without needing to be seen doing it.
cells.core: You're seeing it now, at the very start of it. Something is coming into focus, and because you're tending what's growing, you catch it early — before it's asked for anything, before it's proved itself. That patience is what gives a new thing room to arrive. You're not forcing it; you're just seeing clearly and staying close, and the seeing and the tending are one motion right now.
cells.sheetLine: You're seeing it clearly, and your care is giving it room to arrive.

cells.tense: You're already watching how it will turn out, ahead of the thing itself.
cells.verb: seeing too far ahead of what's actually here
cells.place: in the middle of something you're trying to grow
cells.ask: let one thing stay unfinished and unknown for a day — meet what's actually in front of you, fresh, and what comes back is a light that shines because you are it, not because you proved it.
cells.core: You're already watching how it will turn out, ahead of the thing itself. Every sprout gets measured against the harvest, every small sign read as a verdict. The care is real, but it's turned into management — you're tending the idea of what this will become instead of what's actually in front of you. The pushing is costing you the seeing. You can't perceive what you've already decided.
cells.sheetLine: You're predicting the outcome instead of seeing what's here.

cells.tense: You stopped looking a while back, and you haven't picked the gaze back up.
cells.verb: not letting yourself see what's actually here
cells.place: where something is growing and waiting for you
cells.ask: put your attention on one thing you're building and carry it through to one real, finished step — act from what you see, not from what you feel obliged to, and what comes back is a light that shines because you are it, not because you proved it.
cells.core: You stopped looking a while back, and you haven't picked the gaze back up. Something happened when you did see — maybe it was too much, or it didn't match what you hoped — and since then you've kept your attention elsewhere. The growth is still there, still needing you, but you're not in the room with it. Not looking has become its own kind of protection. The seeing didn't stop existing; you just stopped being the one who does it.
cells.sheetLine: You're not looking, and the thing that needs you is still growing.

cells.tense: You're seeing it already, inside care you're not claiming.
cells.verb: seeing what's growing before you've named it as yours
cells.place: in the care you're already giving
cells.ask: name one thing you've actually seen about what you're tending — say it out loud, once, without proof — and what comes back is a light that shines because you are it, not because you proved it.
cells.core: You're seeing it already, inside care you're not claiming. You notice the first shift, the small opening, the thing that's just beginning — and you call it instinct, or luck, or just being attentive. The seeing is happening, and it's guiding how you tend. But you haven't said, even to yourself, that this clarity is yours. It's running the care quietly, without credit, and you're still describing it as nothing special.
cells.sheetLine: You're already seeing it. You just haven't claimed the seeing.
